html:
SMTO-UI-0028 — SMTO couldn't show how many task slots are free

GUID: c4d2459d-457d-4003-a360-ea22565b6f77
Slug: ui-capacity-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The counter for free task slots received numbers that didn't add up, so it now says "unavailable". This only affects the counter. It doesn't start, stop or change any task.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload this page in your browser (press Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac). If the page was open during an SMTO update, it may be reading the counter in an older way, and a full reload loads the current page.
  2. Before you run or stop anything because of the counter, look at your tasks in the conversation to see what is actually running. This error does not establish whether any task started or finished, so the conversation is the reliable place to check.
  3. If the counter still says "Global run slots: unavailable" after a reload, select Copy error details. The server sent counts SMTO can't display, which only the person who manages SMTO can look into.

What success looks like

  • The counter shows "Global run slots" with real numbers, such as 2/4 free, instead of "unavailable".

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO and mention whether SMTO was updated recently. Don't change settings to try to fix the counter; queued tasks still wait for a free slot as normal.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser rejected the /api/agent/run-capacity response because capacity, available_slots or active_count were not valid integers (or free slots exceeded capacity), so the run-capacity label shows "unavailable".

What this means

  • Task-capacity response contains non-integer or invalid capacity/free/active values, including free slots exceeding capacity. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Task-capacity response contains non-integer or invalid capacity/free/active values, including free slots exceeding capacity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the response values and client/server build compatibility; do not infer that all slots are occupied.

How to fix it

  • native_controls.js refreshCapacity() throws ui_capacity_invalid when GET /api/agent/run-capacity returns non-integer values, capacity < 1, free < 0, free > capacity or active < 0. Inspect that endpoint's response and the server log; a mismatch usually means the browser is running UI files from a different build than the server, so hard-reload the page and confirm both come from the same install.
  • Refresh the task controls. If this repeats, preserve the occurrence and check that the browser and server use compatible builds.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid current counts render without inventing availability.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
